headline: The European Union's technology chief says the bloc's AI law can deal with rogue AI systems, and that Brussels has sent information requests to more than 30 AI companies about their safety measures.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 4: the interview was on 9 Oct 2026 and our 10 Oct edition already carried it (item 87); this copy adds only a few details.
importance_line: People in Europe and the AI companies that sell there are affected, as an EU official says current law can handle rogue AI and that fines of up to 7% of global turnover are possible, but it is her own assessment, no investigation is announced and the companies are not named.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Dunya News, that EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen said in an interview on Friday 9 Oct 2026 that the AI Act, the bloc's risk-based AI law adopted two years ago, can address rogue AI systems because it covers a model's whole life cycle. Our 10 Oct 2026 edition carried the same interview; this version adds that the Commission wrote to more than 30 AI companies in late August and has also asked Chinese AI startups, that its requests could lead to investigations and fines of up to 7% of a company's global yearly turnover, and that she is still assessing the replies.
notes: Repeat: the same Reuters interview was carried in our 10 Oct 2026 edition as item 87 (via thenews.com.pk, score 5); recommend holding this copy back as a duplicate. Read the Reuters text on Dunya News; the Reuters original link is not available, so url is the Dunya page. New details versus the 10 Oct entry: 30-plus companies, 7% fine ceiling, Chinese startups also asked, digital-levy answer.
